::: {.feature-opal}
A loose collection of pitfalls that may be difficult to avoid. In particular,
new users may find these notes useful, but experienced users can also benefit
from them.
:::

::: {.feature-opal}
## Hard Edge Fields

Fields that feature steps, such as hard-edge fringe fields, are strongly
advised against. In sector magnets where particles have different path lengths
inside the magnet, they are kicked one, two, or even more steps differently
depending on position and momentum. Combined with large time steps, this can
lead to visibly split beams and other artificial effects.
:::

::: {.feature-opal}
## Very Short Active Elements / Large Time Steps

This is closely related to the hard-edge problem. It concerns elements that
model electromagnetic devices whose lengths are very short and comparable to
the time step. In this case, a split of the bunch can be observed because some
particles are kicked more often than others. The time step should then be
reduced to mitigate the effect.
:::
